chapter_title: Concerning why Some shall delay to come forth from

fills.notes: The paragraph is enumerating a rule-like sequence ("The second …"), so the lacuna should supply a neutral structural marker rather than any exhortation: an impersonal statement introducing the second case/order.
The verb "fall" in this substrate typically takes a spatial/cosmic object (pit/abyss/depth) rather than a moral one. Here it sets the scene for delay and rescue: a fall into a lower region.
The next clause contrasts with others who depart; thus the first group is defined by remaining with the fallen one. This also matches the closing "and they remain."
The repetition "one … one hour …" reads as a timed interval: "for one …, one hour …"; the smallest connective that makes the Coptic-like cadence work is the prepositional/causal link "for".
The sentence contrasts two sets: some remain and delay; "others who shall …" naturally completes as "depart/go away" in this kind of procedural description.
"They shall delay until they … he is freed" requires a perception/verification verb. In correspondential terms, liberation must be *known/seen* before motion resumes.

fills.fill: the place from which he fell
fills.notes: "come toward …" needs a determinate locus. The tightest correspondential closure is a return toward the originating place/level, matching the opening "fall" and the freeing/restoration sequence.

assessment: Only a small amount of continuous wording survives, but the internal correspondences constrain the sense: a second ‘order’ describing a fall into a lower region, a faithful group that stays, a timed delay, others who depart, waiting until liberation is verified, then returning toward the original place/level. Exact connective particles remain uncertain due to the fragmentary syntax.
